generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL. When the instance is a copy of the compact database, generated PKs start at MAX(existing PK)+1 so they never collide with compact rows. PK columns are exempt from duplicate-share and group-size post-processing.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Draw from the union of compact parent values (schema.original_values[(parent_table, parent_column)]) and generated parent values actually present in the instance; never emit a value absent from that union. For nullable FKs include NULL rows and non-NULL rows. For NOT NULL FKs the pool is never empty (fall back to compact values).
generic_sampling_rules.integer_generic: Uniform integer in [1, 1000]; include boundary values 1, 2, 3 and one step around each listed literal.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_amount: Uniform decimal in [0, 1000] with 2-4 fractional digits; include 0 and values near listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Random person-like name from a small pool; include near-duplicate variants (case, spacing) and exact duplicates for DISTINCT targets.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random short token of 3-15 chars; include near-variants of listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.char_code: Pick from the column's enum pool; include near-variants (case, truncation) of listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Random datetime in 2016-01-01..2018-12-31 formatted '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; respect table date-order rules. Perturbation for distinctness adds/subtracts a timedelta and re-formats with the column format, never string concatenation.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_date: Random integer in [1, 31] representing a day-of-month.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, at least one NULL row per instance; share follows the compact database's observed NULL share for that column (fallback ~10-20% when the compact share is 0). NULLs are planted before distinct-value and FK repair; a planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule.

targets.ties: at least two rows share the max/min rank value

PK column; group-size target realized on join result, not by duplicating PK values

targets.qualifying_rows: >= 2 per group with different non-NULL values
targets.boundary: include max and min distinct values

Next_Claim_Stage_ID self-reference is nullable and only observed value is 1; treated as optional self-FK with pool = compact + generated stage IDs. Policies.Start_Date <= End_Date is contradicted by compact row 151; stated as a soft rule constraining generated rows only, with compact rows exempt. NULLs form their own group for COUNT(DISTINCT) targets and are excluded from the '>= 2 distinct non-NULL values per group' requirement; _ensure_distinct_values is applied after _plant_nulls and is NULL-aware. duplicate_share is interpreted as the fraction of rows that repeat a value (so COUNT(DISTINCT) lies between 50% and 80% of row count). issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows integrity.fk_violations = 89 across the run and validity.new_integrity_failures = 20 (every instance has new integrity failures), yet writer.write_instance_sqlite() DISABLES foreign key enforcement (`con.execute('pragma foreign_keys = OFF')`) before inserting rows. The FK column values are drawn from in-memory generated parent values (fill_foreign_keys_consistently), but the writer never verifies they exist in the actual DB, and the CLI never checks resulting integrity after commit. In addition, rows_skipped is nonzero for Customers (154) and Policies (167), meaning many generated rows were silently rejected (declared PK/UNIQUE collisions from sample_fresh_primary_keys applied only to the generated batch, while PKs restart at 1, colliding with existing compact rows). Combined with FK OFF, the seed parent values referenced by children may be the rejected ones, producing dangling FKs. This directly violates the requirement that dependent-value consistency and integrity be preserved.
issues.request: Enable `pragma foreign_keys = ON` (or verify FKs post-commit) and make the writer/CLI reject or repair rows whose FKs are violated. Fix primary key generation so generated PKs do not collide with existing compact PKs (do not restart at 1 when the compact DB already contains those keys; see same root cause below). After writing, run a referential-integrity check and fail the unit if fk_violations > 0.

issues.evidence: validity.reasons shows compact_rows_missing = 20 for all 20 instances and no_rows_added = 10. The spec says each instance is 'a copy of the compact database plus appended generated rows', and writer copies the compact DB with shutil.copyfile(orig_path, part). However write_instance_sqlite is called from cli._one without passing orig_path (`w = write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p)`) — orig_path defaults to None — so every unit is created from schema.ddl only (`created = True`), and the compact rows are absent from every instance. This is an outright implementation bug contradicting the spec's 'copy of the compact database' statement.
issues.request: Pass the original DB path from the CLI to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p, orig_path=a['orig'])) so each unit is a true copy of the compact database before appended rows. Re-run and confirm compact rows are preserved.

issues.evidence: PK/FK generation restarts at 1 for every generated batch. _spec_sizes builds sizes, samplers for integer PKs fall back to NumberSampler over original values, but generated rows for Customers get rejected 154 times and Policies 167 times (rows_skipped). Because the compact DB is copied in the (intended) design, generated PK values are almost certain to collide with compact PKs. The table_sizes_per_instance values (Customers=15 etc.) are also treated as sizes to append, not as sizes of the final instance, so even a successful copy would not match the spec's per-instance table sizes.
issues.request: Generate PK values disjoint from the existing compact PK range (e.g. start after MAX(existing PK) or use the writer's original rows to seed the sampler), and reduce/generate table sizes so the total per-table row count matches table_sizes_per_instance (do not blindly append 15 more rows on top of the compact DB). Align with the 'copy of the compact database plus appended generated rows' wording — either append rows sized so total equals BASE_SIZES, or document that the sizes are appended.

issues.evidence: claims_documents.Created_Date shows 'generated rows: NULL 0 / 1' and Created_by_Staff_ID 'NULL 0 / 1'. Both are in spec.NULL_TARGETS; the low NULL counts trace to the same writer/PK rejection path (most generated rows for Claims_Documents appear OK but only 1 row was written to some instance). Also, _plant_nulls sets ~10-20% NULL share regardless of the compact DB's actual share, which the interface 7 explicitly asks to follow ('NULL share following the compact database's share for that column'). This is minor (the interface notes nullable columns with NULL 0 / n do not block) but the compact-share rule is not implemented at all.
issues.request: Compute per-column NULL share from the compact DB (schema.original_values) and use it as the sampling target for _plant_nulls, while keeping at least one NULL. Re-run so Claims_Documents nullable columns get at least one NULL; verify no nullable column reports 'NULL 0 / n'.

issues.evidence: The spec's semantic rule section claims Amount_Piad has no formula linking to Amount_Claimed (correct) but 'Amount_Claimed/Amount_Piad >= 0' and non-negativity are enforced only after generation, with no rule for how NULL distinct rows should interact with the rows_with_different_values target. Also, _ensure_distinct_values perturbs only a single value and can be undone by _plant_nulls; the spec says '>= 2 per group with different values' but does not state whether NULL groups count. The construction_pairs: eligible 65, separated 27 (only ~42%) suggests several target patterns only weakly hold. Not blocking, but the interface targets need tightening so the generated instances reliably exercise the aggregate/group-size/distinct targets that the queries depend on.
issues.request: Specify in semantic_rules: (a) whether NULLs form their own group for COUNT(DISTINCT) targets, (b) the concrete 'duplicate_share' in COUNT(DISTINCT c) terms (the value 20-50% is ambiguous between 'rows repeating a value' and 'value counts'), and (c) that _ensure_distinct_values and _plant_nulls must be applied so that at least 2 non-NULL distinct values coexist per group even after NULL planting (order _ensure_distinct_values AFTER _plant_nulls, or make _ensure_distinct_values NULL-aware).

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows large numbers of skipped rows: Policies 53, Claim_Headers 47, Claims_Documents 80, Claims_Processing 120 skipped, while only 18/41/25/47 were added. Two of 20 instances are invalid with reason 'no_rows_added'. The writer (writer.py) inserts generated rows with `INSERT INTO t VALUES (...)` and silently counts failures; the instance builder (instance.py) generates FK values from `instance[pt][pc]` which for parent tables includes only *generated* rows (compact rows are not in `inst`), so FK values are drawn from a pool that may be empty or inconsistent with the compact parent rows actually present in the copied DB. When the parent pool is empty, `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` returns `[None]*n`, which then fails NOT NULL on Policies.Customer_ID / Claim_Headers.Policy_ID / Claims_Processing.Claim_ID, producing the mass skips.
issues.requested_revision: Make FK sampling draw from the union of compact parent values (schema.original_values[(pt,pc)]) and generated parent values, so child rows always reference rows actually present in the copied instance. Ensure the parent pool is never empty for NOT NULL FKs (fall back to compact values). Re-run and confirm rows_skipped is near zero and no instance has 'no_rows_added'.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_reserve_childless_parents` sets a child FK value to None to create a childless parent: `cvals[i] = None`. For NOT NULL FK columns (Policies.Customer_ID, Claim_Headers.Policy_ID, Claims_Processing.Claim_ID) this produces a NOT NULL violation and the row is skipped by the writer. This directly conflicts with the spec's `child_rows_with_null_fk: false` target for these columns.
issues.requested_revision: Do not plant NULL into NOT NULL FK columns. Instead, ensure childless parents by leaving at least one parent PK unreferenced (e.g. reserve a parent PK value and exclude it from the child FK draw), never by nulling a NOT NULL child FK.

issues.evidence: spec.py lists `('Policies','Policy_ID')` in DISTINCT_COLUMNS and `('Customers','Customer_ID')` in GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS, but these are primary keys. `_apply_duplicate_share` and `_apply_group_sizes` mutate these columns after PK assignment, which can create duplicate PKs (later dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys only for the pre-post-processing pass, not after). The spec's per-column exceptions for Policy_ID and Customer_ID only require `unmatched_join_rows` / `group_sizes` on the *join* result, not duplicate PK values. Applying duplicate-share/group-size to a PK column is a spec/program mismatch and risks PK collisions.
issues.requested_revision: Remove PK columns from DISTINCT_COLUMNS and GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS; realize the group-size/unmatched-join targets on the join result (e.g. via child FK distribution) rather than by duplicating PK values. Alternatively, re-run sample_fresh_primary_keys after post-processing and document that PKs are exempt from duplicate-share.

issues.evidence: The spec's `supporting_evidence` for `Policies.Start_Date <= End_Date` admits the compact row 151 violates the rule (2017-12-20 > 2017-09-16) and calls it a 'soft order rule'. The program's `_enforce_date_order` swaps start/end for generated rows, but the compact violating row remains in every copied instance, so the rule does not hold on the instance as a whole. The spec should state clearly whether the rule is a hard constraint (then the compact row must be excluded or the rule dropped) or a soft rule (then it should not be listed as a semantic rule).
issues.requested_revision: Either drop the Start_Date <= End_Date rule from semantic_rules_and_formulas (since it is contradicted by compact data), or state it explicitly as a soft rule that only constrains generated rows and document that compact rows are exempt. Do not present it as a hard semantic rule.

issues.evidence: The spec's `uncertainty` notes that `Next_Claim_Stage_ID` self-reference 'only observed value is 1' and is treated as optional self-FK, but the semantic rule `Next_Claim_Stage_ID IS NULL OR Next_Claim_Stage_ID IN (SELECT Claim_Stage_ID FROM Claims_Processing_Stages)` is listed as a hard formula. With Claims_Processing_Stages size 2 and INT_ENUMS only [1,3] for Claim_Stage_ID, the self-FK pool is small; the program's `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` for self-FK uses `instance[t][pc]` which is the generated PK list, but the compact stage rows (if any) are not included, so the self-FK may reference a stage ID not present in the copied instance. This is a dependency-consistency gap.
issues.requested_revision: Include compact parent values in the self-FK pool (same fix as issue 1) and confirm the self-FK rule holds on the full instance. If the compact DB has no Claims_Processing_Stages rows, document that the self-FK is generated-only and the rule is vacuously satisfied.

issues.evidence: `_ensure_distinct_values` is applied to `Policies.Start_Date` (in DIFFERENT_VALUE_COLUMNS) after `_plant_nulls`, but it only perturbs a value if all non-NULL values are equal. For datetime strings it appends 'x' (`vals[i] = v + 'x'`), producing an invalid datetime string that violates the `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S` format target and the date-order rule. This is a latent bug that can corrupt Start_Date values.
issues.requested_revision: For datetime columns, perturb by adding/subtracting a timedelta and re-formatting with spec.DATE_FMT, not by string concatenation. Re-apply `_enforce_date_order` after any perturbation.

issues.evidence: `_apply_duplicate_share` and `_apply_group_sizes` are applied to `Claims_Processing.Claim_Stage_ID` and `Claims_Processing_Stages.Claim_Status_Name`, but these columns are also FK targets (Claim_Stage_ID is referenced by Claims_Processing.Claim_Stage_ID and Next_Claim_Stage_ID). Mutating Claim_Stage_ID after FK assignment can break the FK (child references a stage ID no longer present). The self-FK fix loop in `build_random_instance` only runs for `pt == t`, not for cross-table FK to Claims_Processing_Stages.
issues.requested_revision: Apply group-size/duplicate-share to FK-target columns before FK assignment, or re-validate and repair FKs after post-processing. Ensure Claims_Processing.Claim_Stage_ID and Next_Claim_Stage_ID always reference existing Claims_Processing_Stages.Claim_Stage_ID values.
